sources.entry: Redash - Connect and query your data sources, build dashboards to visualize data and share them with your company. (Source Code) BSD-2-Clause Docker
Redash | Make sense of your data

summary.one_liner: Redash is a browser-based tool for writing SQL and NoSQL queries against many data sources, visualizing the results, building dashboards, and sharing them with a team.
summary.what_it_does: Redash runs in the browser and provides a query editor with a schema browser and auto-complete for composing SQL and NoSQL queries. Query results can be turned into visualizations by drag and drop and combined into dashboards. Queries and visualizations can be shared by URL so colleagues can review them. Charts and dashboards can be refreshed on a schedule, and alerts can be defined to fire when data meets set conditions. Everything available in the UI is also exposed through a REST API. The README lists more than 35 built-in data sources, including PostgreSQL, MySQL, Snowflake, BigQuery, Elasticsearch, MongoDB, and Google Sheets, and says the data source API is extensible.
use_cases: query multiple databases from one browser interface
build shared dashboards for a company
alert when data crosses a threshold
share SQL queries and reports for peer review
visualize data from warehouses like BigQuery or Snowflake
how_to_run: Set up a Redash instance (the README links to ready-made AWS/GCE images and setup documentation)
notable: Connects to more than 35 built-in SQL and NoSQL data sources, with an extensible data source API
Schema browser and auto-complete in the query editor
Every UI action is available through the REST API
caveats: The README does not describe installation requirements or resource needs; it points to external setup docs and images
Hosted-service or paid tier details are not mentioned in the README
